annotations.text:
Production today. One Sales Representative field under Service Advisor.

Measured gaps: Lead Technician to Service Advisor 36px; Service Advisor to Sales Representative 16px.
Production today. A plain list: Unassigned, then every active sales representative.

Plain text, like Lead Technician and Service Advisor: "Sales Representative", reading "Unassigned". No box and no buttons at rest.

Measured gaps: 16px, 16px.

Lead Technician reads blank here on first load; production does the same (board 1.0). It is not part of this project.
Hovering the rep row shows the field box with its dropdown arrow, and the grey + beside it.
"Unassigned" is the first option, checked when nobody is picked, then every active sales representative.
Becky Gonzales is the Sales Representative, shown as plain text. She gets credit for the whole job: labor, parts and shop supplies.
With a person in the field, hovering shows the same box and arrow, and the + beside the row. To clear it, pick "Unassigned" from the list (decision 69).
Tooltip: "Add representative".
The menu lists the one row a work order can add: "Sales Representative - Parts".

Two rows, "Sales Representative - Labor" and "Sales Representative - Parts", both reading Becky Gonzales: the added row starts with the person the work order already credits (decision 65), so adding it alone moves no credit. No list opens on its own.

Labels show in full. Measured gaps: 16px, 16px, 16px.

Both boxes show at once, each with its arrow. With Labor and Parts showing, the arrow sits on the name line in the bottom corner (decision 70). The + is gone (nothing left to add); the Parts row has a grey x beside it that removes the row.

With Labor and Parts showing, the arrow sits on the name line in the bottom corner (decision 70). Each row has the same list: Unassigned first, then the reps. A person already on the other row is not hidden (decision 67).
Daniel Montoya sold the labor, Becky Gonzales the parts. On the invoice and in Sales By Representative, each gets only their own side; shop supplies ride with Labor.
Tooltip: "Remove Sales Representative - Parts". With Labor and Parts showing, the arrow sits on the name line in the bottom corner (decision 70).
Removing the Parts row leaves the Labor person, Daniel Montoya, as the one Sales Representative for the whole job (decision 66). Becky is not put back.
To clear the field, open its list and pick "Unassigned", the first option (decision 69). Daniel Montoya is checked as the current rep.
After picking Unassigned the field reads "Unassigned": nobody gets credit for this work order unless the customer fallback applies at invoicing.

Invoiced work order S2-17540 with two reps. The rows are plain text: "Sales Representative - Labor" Daniel Montoya, "Sales Representative - Parts" Becky Gonzales. Measured gaps: 16px, 16px, 16px (decision 47).

Hovering the rows changes nothing: no box, no arrow, no + and no remove x (checked in the browser: zero buttons on the card; the hovered screenshot is identical to this one).
Production today. A rep change does not appear in the log.

Each change is a "Sales representative changed" entry with who, when, and before → after. Adding Parts: "Becky Gonzales → Becky Gonzales (Parts) · Becky Gonzales (Labor)". Removing it: "Becky Gonzales (Parts) · Daniel Montoya (Labor) → Daniel Montoya". Clearing: "Daniel Montoya → Unassigned". (Test entries from building this canvas fill the list.)

WORK ORDER CARD: ONE REP, ADD, REMOVE

Read left to right. Boards marked Before are production today. Every other board is the build, on work order S2-17528 (invoiced S2-17540 for the read-only boards).

One "Sales Representative" field. At rest the rows are plain text. Hovering the rep rows shows every field's box and dropdown arrow, and the buttons beside the rows: a + beside the first row (tooltip "Add representative") and an x beside an added row (tooltip "Remove Sales Representative - Parts").

Buttons: the design system's Tertiary button, small icon-only size, 32px square, 8px corners, grey Lucide icon, light fill on hover.

Spacing rule (decision 47): the vertical gap between Lead Technician, Service Advisor and every Sales Representative field is 16px, one field or two. Measured on these boards: 16px every time. Production today has 36px between Lead Technician and Service Advisor.

To clear a field, pick "Unassigned", first in every list; it is the only way to clear (decision 69).
Production today. One Sales Representative, or N/A.
Production today. One Sales Representative dropdown.
Production today. New Customer has no Sales Representative field.
One outlined "Sales Representative" field reading "Unassigned", with the + beside it.
Unassigned, then the reps.
Christian Wallace is the customer's one rep: Service Labor, Service Parts and Part Sales all go to him. To clear it, pick "Unassigned" from the list (decision 69).
Tooltip: "Add representative".
"Sales Representative - Service Parts" and "Sales Representative - Part Sales".

The first field is renamed "Sales Representative - Service Labor". The new "Sales Representative - Service Parts" row starts with the same person (Christian Wallace), so adding it alone moves no credit, and its list does not open on its own. It has a remove x beside it.
Service Parts is already added, so the menu lists only "Sales Representative - Part Sales".
Service Labor, Service Parts and Part Sales; Service Parts and Part Sales each have a remove x. The + is gone: nothing left to add. Part Sales also starts with the person already credited.
Jason Garrison is picked for Service Parts. The Part Sales list is the same as every other: Unassigned first, then the reps. No "Same as Service Parts" option.
Christian Wallace for Service Labor, Jason Garrison for Service Parts, Dylan Rush for Part Sales.
Tooltip: "Remove Sales Representative - Service Parts".

Service Parts removed: the Service Labor person (Christian Wallace) is the one "Sales Representative" again, and Part Sales keeps its own row (Dylan Rush). A customer can have its own Part Sales rep without splitting service. The + is back, offering Service Parts.

Removing the Part Sales row puts part sales back on the Service Parts person (or the one rep).

Service Parts added back (Jason Garrison) and saved. The customer page shows the same rows as the window, as plain text: Service Labor Christian Wallace, Service Parts Jason Garrison, Part Sales Dylan Rush.
Decision 34: New Customer gets the same optional Sales Representative field and +, in the same spot as on Edit Customer.
The same two options as Edit Customer. (A name is typed so the window shows no required-field message.)
Part Sales added on its own: "Sales Representative" and "Sales Representative - Part Sales", with its remove x. Same rows and rules as Edit Customer.

A CUSTOMER'S REPS: EDIT CUSTOMER AND NEW CUSTOMER

The customer's reps are the defaults for its new work orders and part sales. Read left to right.

Boards marked Before are production today. Every other board is the build, on Gonsoulin Diesel Services Inc.

In the customer window the fields are outlined like every other field, and the + and remove x always show (no hover needed). The + menu offers "Sales Representative - Service Parts" and "Sales Representative - Part Sales", each only until it is added. There is no "Same as Service Parts" option.

Test data note: this local copy is anonymized, so the customer window lists the reps by their login names (Christian Wallace, Jason Garrison, Dylan Rush) while the work order card shows their staff names. Production uses one name per person.
Production today. The part sale card has no Sales Representative field.

One "Sales Representative" field on the part sale card, plain text at rest, the full width of the card. The part sale field belongs to Part Sales Update v1 (SV-10266) and looks exactly as that feature builds it; Split Representatives changes nothing about it (decision 71). No + button, no remove x.
Part Sales Update v1's own hover box and arrow, the full width of the card.
Part Sales Update v1's list, unchanged by this project. The rep on the part sale when it is invoiced gets the credit.
Gerald Ortiz picked. The same field, still no + button and no remove x.

A PART SALE'S REP

The part sale field belongs to Part Sales Update v1 (SV-10266) and looks exactly as that feature builds it; Split Representatives changes nothing about it (decision 71). No + button, no remove x.

A part sale has one Sales Representative. Read left to right. Board 3.0 is production today. Boards 3.1 to 3.4 are the build, on part sale P2-204.
Production today. A "Product Type" filter. Each invoice is credited whole to its one rep.
Production today. Part Sales or Service Sales.
Production today. No Sales Type column.
Production today. One row per invoice under each rep.

The filter is now "Sales Type". Devon 3 invoices, $1,314.68; Elliot 3 invoices, $2,788.81; total $4,103.49. A split invoice counts once for each rep who sold part of it; the totals do not change because of a split.
Decision 40: the Sales Type column is off by default on screen. S1-12 appears under both reps: Devon with its parts, Elliot with its labor and shop supplies. A side a rep did not sell shows a dash.
Labor, Parts and Part Sales, all on by default. Rows and every total follow it; any combination works.
"Sales Type: Labor" keeps only the labor side of each work order. (The Sales Type column is switched on in this board, from board 4.9.)
Sales Type is the first entry, off by default.
Switching it on adds the column next to Status.

Values: Labor, Parts and Part Sales. One rep with both sides of one work order shows as one row reading "Labor, Parts" (S1-32, decision 38). S1-12: Devon "Parts" ($266.18), Elliot "Labor" ($2,186.82), shop supplies ($175.50) with Labor (decision 37).

At 1600px wide, the columns after Parts Margin scroll under the pinned Subtotal; production behaves the same.
Downloaded with the Sales Type column switched off on screen: the file still has Sales Type (decision 40). An empty side is a blank cell. (Shown as a spreadsheet would open it.)
The PDF always has the Sales Type column. An empty side shows a dash. Header lines name the filters, including "Sales Type: All".

SALES BY REPRESENTATIVE REPORT

Each rep is credited only for the side they sold. Read left to right.

Boards marked Before are production today (Staging Heavy Duty data). Every other board is the build, Last 12 months: S1-12 split (Devon Parts, Elliot Labor), S1-32 Devon alone, and part sales P1-9006, P1-4 and P1-9005.
Production today: "Product Type: All products", options Part Sales and Service Sales.
"Sales Type: All Sales", same options (Part Sales, Service Sales) and same behavior. Sales By Customer keeps whole invoices; it does not split by rep.

The filter open. Options read Part Sales and Service Sales; with both selected it reads Sales Type: All Sales (S8-R6 to S8-R8).

At 1600px wide, Adjustments and Margin scroll under the pinned Subtotal; the report behaves the same way on Sales By Representative (board 4.10).

SALES BY CUSTOMER: THE FILTER NAME

Only the filter's wording changes, to match Sales By Representative. Board 5.0 is production today; 5.1 and 5.2 are the build (Staging Heavy Duty data, Date: Last 12 months).
Production today. On a phone the work order card sits behind the details panel.
Production today. The same one-person list as on a computer.
"Sales Representative" reading "Unassigned", with the + always showing beside it.
The native dropdown, the same as Lead Technician: Unassigned first, then the reps.
Becky Gonzales. The + shows without any hover.
The menu: "Sales Representative - Parts".
"Sales Representative - Labor" and "Sales Representative - Parts", both Becky; labels in full; the Parts row has its remove x, always showing. At rest the rows read as plain text.
The same list per row. With Labor and Parts showing, the arrow sits on the name line in the bottom corner (decision 70).

ON A PHONE

The same field and the same rules on a 390px-wide touch screen. Read left to right.

Boards 6.0 and 6.1 are production today; 6.2 to 6.7 are the build, on S2-17528.

There is no hover on a phone, so the + and remove x always show. To clear a field, pick "Unassigned" from its list (decision 69). Tapping a field opens the native dropdown, like Lead Technician (decision 48).
